_meta.source: South African Police Service — Crime Statistics
_meta.update_frequency: Annual (September each year, for Apr–Mar financial year)
_meta.notes: SAPS publishes crime stats once per year in September. No public API. Data must be manually extracted from the published Excel workbooks. Latest annual: 2023/24. Quarterly Jan-Mar 2022 to 2026 checked 2026-10-28 from newdatasets/2025-2026_-_4th_Quarter_WEB.xlsx (scripts/crime/import_quarter.py) and held in _meta.pending_statistics: the workbook has no annual totals and no release date. Update by running: python scripts/update_crime.py (manual step required — see script comments)
_meta.public_notes: Annual figures for the 2023/24 financial year (April to March), from the South African Police Service. SAPS also publishes quarterly figures. Its figures for January to March 2026, with the same months in 2022 to 2025, have been checked and will be shown as a separate quarterly series once their release date is confirmed. They cover one quarter, so they cannot be compared with the annual totals. SAPS annual figures newer than 2023/24 have not been added.

pending_statistics.reason: Checked against the SAPS workbook on 2026-10-28 but not shown: the workbook does not state a release date. Run scripts/crime/import_quarter.py with --released once it is confirmed.

statistics.title: Contact crimes reported to the police, January to March
statistics.description: Contact crimes (crimes against the person) reported to SAPS in January to March 2026, the fourth quarter of the 2025/26 financial year. SAPS counts murder, sexual offences, attempted murder, assault with intent to inflict grievous bodily harm, common assault, common robbery and robbery with aggravating circumstances. One quarter, not a full year.

statistics.title: Murders reported to the police
statistics.description: Total murder cases reported nationally for the 2023/24 financial year (April 2023 – March 2024). This is the first decline in four years, equating to approximately 72 murders per day. The rate is 41.9 per 100,000 population.

statistics.title: Contact crimes reported to the police
statistics.description: Contact crimes include assault GBH, common assault, robbery with aggravating circumstances, common robbery, sexual offences, and murder. Total contact crimes declined for the 2023/24 reporting period.

statistics.title: Robbery with aggravating circumstances
statistics.description: Robberies involving a weapon, violence, or the threat of violence for the 2023/24 financial year. This category includes carjacking, truck hijacking, house robbery, and bank robbery.
